audience: Engineers seeking the relationship between DFlash parallel draft distributions and DDTree target verification.
prerequisites: Products and sums of small probabilities.
objective: Relate parallel marginal proposals to a budgeted prefix tree and distinguish draft coverage from target-selected committed output.
scope: All thirty narration blocks of the combined example, including seven loop-generated selections and the repaired factorization equations; no automatic approval of rendered graphics.
assumptions: Q1, Q2 and Q3 are toy distributions under fixed shared conditioning.
The root b is an already-emitted anchor and is outside the seven-node proposal budget.
The expected-depth prefix sum is under Q, not a guarantee under the target distribution.
Insertion order is not BFS. Position depth, ancestor visibility and target membership have distinct roles.
Runtime improvement depends on draft, tree-build and verification costs per committed token; accepting two proposals is not measured speedup.
unknowns: No expected visual events, audiovisual review or learner responses are supplied. Managed timeline support is implemented, but a rendered timeline must still be provided for comparison.
The opening's target-call claim is a motivation, not a measured latency guarantee. Performance depends on all costs and actual target reuse as qualified in the closing beats.

claims.statement: A finite budget buys alternative prefixes scored under factorized Q rather than only one modal path.

evidence.support: The surrogate maximizes expected matched depth under Q using prefix masses; root does not count toward B.

claims.statement: A target miss terminates cached reuse but is appended as valid output and the next anchor.

evidence.locator: follow_verified_tree; ddtree_generate accepted_tokens and next_token output assignments
evidence.support: The first nonmember next_token is returned separately and written after matched tokens; only matched indices retain current target KV entries.

claims.statement: The worked seventh prefix a-model-works has exact mass 0.1092; rounded 0.109 is approximate.

evidence.support: The input values 0.35, 0.60 and 0.52 yield the independently checked exact product.

claims.statement: DFlash concatenates selected target hidden states, projects them and uses their keys and values in every draft layer for noncausal parallel block prediction.

evidence.locator: extract_context_feature; DFlashDraftModel.forward; Qwen3DFlashAttention.forward; dflash_generate draft call
evidence.support: The target features are concatenated, normalized/projected, and passed into each layer's k_ctx/v_ctx; draft inference sets is_causal=False and predicts all masked positions.

claims.statement: A flat array retains node identity through depth-based positions and ancestor/self visibility, not array adjacency.

evidence.support: Each row inherits parent visibility plus self. Position IDs add start to node depths. This separates sibling branches in one target input.

claims.statement: The episode's throughput discussion requires draft, tree-build and verification costs per actual committed token; a larger Q-surrogate score alone is not measured speedup.

evidence.support: The displayed formula divides draft plus tree-build plus verify time by committed tokens; narration also names growing attention/cache-compaction work.

worked_examples.description: Preserve exact arithmetic despite rounded visual labels.
Reconstruct tree membership from token-array paths and supplied target choices; root b is excluded from new output.
Independently derive the scene's eight-position visibility matrix from token-array ancestry, not its hand-written mask constants.

beats.purpose: Contrast serial target work with opportunities for reuse, without a measured speedup claim.

narration.text: The expensive target model normally advances one token per decode pass. Speculative decoding wins only when one target pass commits several tokens.

beats.purpose: Connect cheap block drafting to multiple likely continuations.

narration.text: DFlash makes drafting cheap by predicting a whole block in parallel. DDTree then spends the verifier budget on several likely continuations, instead of betting everything on one path.

beats.purpose: Distinguish the emitted bonus from a token already processed by the target.

narration.text: Each round starts with a bonus token, shown in yellow. The target selected it previously, but has not yet processed it. DFlash appends masked future positions after that token.

beats.purpose: Ground shared draft conditioning in projected target features.

narration.text: The previous target pass exposes hidden states from several layers. DFlash concatenates and projects them, then injects the result as keys and values into every small draft layer. The drafter therefore reuses the target's rich context instead of reasoning from scratch.

beats.purpose: Label invented probability columns produced by one parallel draft pass.

narration.text: One non-causal draft pass predicts all masked positions simultaneously. Our toy pass returns these three probability distributions. These values are invented for the example, but every later calculation uses them exactly.

beats.purpose: Distinguish target conditionals from draft marginals.

narration.text: The target distribution is path-conditioned. Its distribution for position three depends on the actual tokens chosen at positions one and two.

beats.purpose: Build correctly scoped one-, two-, and three-token prefix products.

narration.text: A single DFlash pass cannot provide those conditionals. It provides one marginal per position, all conditioned on the same earlier context and bonus token. DDTree deliberately uses the factorized approximation Q: multiply the appropriate marginal at each depth.

beats.purpose: Show one modal draft continuation.

narration.text: Vanilla DFlash collapses each column to one token. Here that creates the single proposal: the, model, works.

beats.purpose: Use the first target miss to motivate retaining a.

narration.text: If the target chooses a at the first position, verification stops immediately, even though the drafter assigned a substantial thirty-five percent mass. DDTree keeps alternatives when they are worth the node budget.

beats.purpose: Relate matched depth to the sum of depth-reaching probabilities.

narration.text: The objective is expected matched depth. A useful identity avoids heavy math: for any nonnegative integer length, its expectation is the chance of reaching depth one, plus the chance of reaching depth two, and so on.

beats.purpose: Qualify the prefix-mass sum under the factorized draft distribution.

narration.text: In a prefix-closed tree, reaching a particular depth means matching one node at that depth. Under the factorized draft distribution, each node contributes exactly its prefix probability. So the objective is simply the sum of all node masses.

beats.purpose: Explain why strict-probability extensions cannot outrank parents.

narration.text: Every child multiplies its parent mass by a probability below one. Therefore a child can never outrank its parent. Taking the B highest-mass prefixes automatically includes every required ancestor.

beats.purpose: Offer a sibling and best child instead of enumerating the full vocabulary tree.

narration.text: Now build the tree without enumerating the vocabulary cubed. A max-heap starts with the best depth-one token. Each pop inserts that prefix into the tree, then offers at most two new candidates: its next sibling, and its best child.

beats.purpose: Select the highest first-token mass.

narration.text: First comes the with mass point five five. The heap now contains its next sibling, a, and its best child, the-model.

beats.purpose: Choose breadth before a lower-mass deep path.

narration.text: Next is a at point three five. Notice that it beats the-model at point three three, so breadth can be more valuable than depth.

beats.purpose: Compute a prefix from parent and marginal.

narration.text: Then the-model: point five five times point six equals point three three. Products are the path scores.

beats.purpose: Retain the second branch by joint mass.

narration.text: Then a-model at point two one. This branch is retained because its joint mass still exceeds the remaining alternatives.

beats.purpose: Mark the depth-three product as rounded.

narration.text: The best depth-three prefix is the-model-works: point three three times point five two, or about point one seven two.

beats.purpose: Return to a shallower prefix when its mass is next.

narration.text: The-system follows at point one six five. It is slightly below the deeper works prefix, so the heap ordering decides their insertion.

beats.purpose: Complete the seven-node proposal budget.

narration.text: Finally a-model-works enters at point one zero nine. Seven pops fill the budget. The selected prefixes are globally the seven largest under Q.

beats.purpose: Separate surrogate optimality from unavailable target conditionals.

narration.text: This optimality is precise but limited. The tree is optimal for the factorized DFlash surrogate Q. It is not claimed to be optimal for the target's unavailable path-conditioned distribution p.

beats.purpose: Retain distinct token-node identities and depth positions in the flat input.

narration.text: The target model receives a flat token array, not a pointer-based tree. Duplicate token labels remain distinct nodes because they have different parents. Position IDs come from tree depth, not flat array index.

beats.purpose: Root, ancestors and self define each visible row.

narration.text: Tree attention restores the semantics. Every node may attend to the committed context, its ancestors, and itself, but never to a sibling or another branch. For example, node five, works, sees root b, the, model, and itself.

beats.purpose: Compute target continuation distributions across all valid prefix positions once.

narration.text: That mask lets one causal target-model forward pass compute the correct next token distribution after every candidate prefix in parallel.

beats.purpose: Let the target's root decision select the a branch.

narration.text: Verification starts at the bonus-token root. The target applies its own decoding rule there. In this example it chooses a, so the walk takes the a edge. The drafter's probabilities do not make this decision.

beats.purpose: Reuse a second matching child from cached logits.

narration.text: At node a, the already-computed target logits choose model. That child exists, so the second speculative token is accepted too.

beats.purpose: Commit matched a/model followed by the missing target token runs.

narration.text: At a-model, the target chooses runs. That child was not in our seven-node tree, so the walk stops. The matched nodes a and model are committed. Runs is also committed as the next bonus token, ready for the following round.

beats.purpose: Relate parallel drafting to extra verification coverage.

narration.text: The system trade-off is now clear. DFlash avoids token-by-token draft latency by predicting the block in parallel. DDTree uses extra verifier width, controlled by B, to raise the expected number of committed tokens.

beats.purpose: Require benefits to outweigh construction, attention and compaction costs.

narration.text: A larger tree is not free: tree construction, attention, and cache compaction grow with the budget. The useful operating point is where extra accepted tokens still outweigh that wider verification pass.

beats.purpose: End with target-selected output rather than draft-score authority.

narration.text: Most importantly, DDTree changes where the target looks, not what the target chooses. Every committed token is selected by the target model's own decoding rule. The tree only increases the chance that several of those choices were already waiting in the same verification pass.

transfer_questions.question: If increasing B improves the sum of draft prefix masses, has it proved lower wall-clock time per output token?
transfer_questions.expected_answer: No. The sum is a Q-based coverage surrogate. Drafting, tree construction, verification cost and actual target-selected output must also be considered.
transfer_questions.justification: A larger nonnegative prefix sum cannot establish a runtime inequality. The denominator is actual committed tokens, whereas the numerator includes work that generally increases with tree size. The paper distinguishes the surrogate from the target objective.

transfer_questions.question: Why is runs emitted even though it is not a child of a-model?
transfer_questions.expected_answer: Because the target selected it at that prefix. Only cached continuation stops; the token remains valid output and anchors the next round.
transfer_questions.justification: Direct membership testing reaches [a,model], finds no [a,model,runs], and returns runs separately. The official output assignment appends that returned token.
